clue.text: Understood to have won popularity

definitions.meaning: grasped an idea, got the point
became fashionable, as a craze does

explanation.surface: Someone realises that they have become popular.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both grasped a meaning and became widely fashionable.

clue.text: Like to have US currency rise

parts.note: as means like, in the sense of similar to
a cent is a coin of American money

explanation.surface: Something resembling the dollar going up in value.
explanation.definitionFit: A climb or upward movement is a synonym, as in a balloon's slow climb.

clue.text: Sod the informer!

definitions.meaning: a piece of turf, the green lawn covering
British slang for a police informant, one who tells on others

explanation.surface: An outburst cursing the person who betrayed the gang to the police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sod' looks like a British swear word; it is the turf. A grass in British slang is someone who informs to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Turf is lawn vegetation, and British slang names a police informant the same way.

clue.text: Harrier finds common soldiers trapped between two hills

indicators.note: the soldiers are caught in the middle, so they go inside the pair of hills
two asks for the hill word to be written twice

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, common on Dartmoor
men are ordinary soldiers as against officers

explanation.surface: A Harrier jet spots troops pinned down in a valley between two hills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harrier' suggests the jump-jet or the hawk, but here it is one who harries or pesters.
explanation.definitionFit: To harry is to harass persistently, so a harrier is a persecutor who torments.

clue.text: Another thing that is useful for a woman in retirement

definitions.text: Another thing that is useful for a woman in retirement

parts.words: Another thing that is useful for a woman in retirement
parts.note: retirement here means going to bed for the night, not leaving work, so the useful thing is a garment worn to sleep

explanation.surface: A list of handy items for a woman who has stopped working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retirement' suggests ending a career, but retiring is also going to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's nightdress is the garment worn on retiring to bed.

clue.text: Personal attractions do damage in the Civil Service

indicators.note: the damage word is placed inside the abbreviation for the service

parts.note: CS is the standard abbreviation for the Civil Service
to harm is to do damage

explanation.surface: Someone's appeal causes trouble within government departments.
explanation.definitionFit: Appealing personal qualities that allure others are synonyms.

clue.text: Fellow-archdeacon exposes a lot of witches

parts.note: co- is the prefix meaning fellow or joint, as in co-worker
Ven, short for Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon

explanation.surface: One clergyman reveals to another a gathering of witches.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathering or band of witches, traditionally thirteen, is called this.

clue.text: Bill takes it up in a hostile environment

indicators.note: an environment surrounds, so the hostile word encloses the other piece

parts.note: adverse means hostile or unfavourable

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the little word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A bill is pushed through against fierce opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the little word in this down clue. 'Bill' looks like a noun (a law, an invoice) but is a verb: to bill a show is to publicise it.
explanation.definitionFit: To bill an act is to publicise or promote it, as on a playbill or poster.

clue.text: Instructions suggesting that female must not arrange trysts

definitions.text: suggesting that female must not arrange trysts
definitions.meaning: read as two words, the male is the one who makes the romantic appointments

explanation.surface: Rules say a woman may not set up romantic meetings.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as MAN DATES, it says the man, not the woman, fixes the trysts.
explanation.definitionFit: Authoritative commands or orders are synonyms, as a government has electoral authority to act.

clue.text: What pastry-lovers may consume in a City hideaway

parts.note: EC is the postcode of the City of London
a lair is an animal's den, a hiding place

explanation.surface: Something cake fans might eat in a secret den in the financial district.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is the financial district of London, whose postcodes begin EC.
explanation.definitionFit: A cream-filled choux finger is a pastry treat such people enjoy.

clue.text: US soldier opposed to sporting contest has to let off steam

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
v, short for versus, means against
an event is a competition at a sports meeting

explanation.surface: An American soldier, against a sports fixture, has to release frustration.
explanation.definitionFit: To express pent-up feelings openly is the idiom's meaning.

clue.text: A saint we recollect when agitated

indicators.note: read as re-collect, gathering the letters together again in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone remembers a holy figure while flustered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recollect' looks like remember; split as re-collect it signals the letters of A SAINT WE are regrouped.
explanation.definitionFit: Being anxious or flustered is the idiom's sense, as if perspiring from nerves.

clue.text: Standard behaviour by an adversary of the Saxons

parts.note: a norm is the usual, expected pattern of behaviour
taken as written

explanation.surface: The typical conduct of an enemy of the Anglo-Saxons.
explanation.walkthrough: The Normans conquered the Anglo-Saxons in 1066.
explanation.definitionFit: The invaders from Normandy defeated the Anglo-Saxon English at Hastings.

clue.text: China may be protected by top MPs' place

definitions.meaning: fine porcelain is kept safe behind glass in a piece of furniture
senior ministers sit as members of the government's inner council

explanation.surface: Diplomatic relations with China are safeguarded by senior politicians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country; it is porcelain kept in a display cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Porcelain is stored in a glass-fronted cupboard, and senior ministers serve on the government's top body.

clue.text: At one's peak during the A Level year

definitions.meaning: pupils sit A Levels, the final school exams, in the senior class

explanation.surface: A student is at their best in the final year of school.
explanation.walkthrough: A Levels are the exams British pupils take at about eighteen, in the highest school year, once called the top form.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in excellent condition is the idiom; a school's senior class sits the final exams.

clue.text: Change one's opinion and go to a boxing-match

parts.note: a bout is a fight in boxing
a turn is a go, as in taking one's turn

explanation.surface: Someone changes their mind and heads off to see a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A reversal of policy or view is named after the soldier's command to face the other way.

clue.text: Fine wool for Her Majesty the Queen in a piece of luggage

indicators.note: the royal abbreviations are packed inside the luggage word

parts.note: a case is a suitcase
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A fine woollen garment for the monarch packed in a suitcase.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft goat hair from Kashmir is a luxury fibre for knitwear.

clue.text: Coup causes teacher to have apoplexy

parts.note: a master is a schoolteacher
apoplexy is an old word for a seizure or brain haemorrhage

explanation.surface: An upheaval makes a schoolteacher have a seizure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coup' suggests a seizure of power; here it is a brilliant success.
explanation.definitionFit: A brilliant, decisive move or achievement is a synonym.

clue.text: Try to hold emperor causing violent disturbance

indicators.note: the trial word holds the emperor abbreviation within it

parts.note: to test is to try
EMP is an abbreviation of emperor

explanation.surface: An attempt to detain an emperor causes a riot.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent storm, or figuratively an uproar, is meant.

clue.text: A terrible blunder has made him weep bitterly

definitions.meaning: one who wails loudly, crying out in pain or grief

explanation.surface: A dreadful error has reduced a man to tears.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is one who wails, as a wolf or weeping person does.
explanation.definitionFit: A glaring mistake is a synonym, and one who wails loudly is literally so named.

clue.text: Interrupt to contribute cash

definitions.meaning: to pay a share towards a collection

explanation.surface: Someone cuts in to offer money.
explanation.definitionFit: To butt into talk, or to add one's share of money, are both this phrasal verb.

clue.text: Nine players find empty goalposts

parts.note: with no contents, as if nothing is there
the net hangs from the goalposts, standing for the goal

explanation.surface: A nine-strong team find the opposing goal unguarded.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of nine musicians, or a composition for them, is so called.

clue.text: It carries strikers to a competition fight

parts.note: a match is a contest or game
to box is to fight with fists

explanation.surface: A team bus takes its forwards to a boxing contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strikers' suggests footballers; they are matches, struck to light.
explanation.definitionFit: A small container holds the safety sticks that are struck to make fire.

clue.text: An ambassador needs skill and compassion

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador
art is skill, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.surface: A diplomat must have tact and sympathy.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling for others, as in a kind heart, is meant.

clue.text: Condemn the simpleton who holds one back

indicators.note: the fool grips the number inside him

parts.note: a dunce is a slow-witted person

indicators.note: back means the number word is read from right to left

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone rebukes a fool who is restraining a person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ONE into ENO, which DUNCE holds.
explanation.definitionFit: To denounce is to criticise publicly or accuse, a synonym of condemning.

clue.text: Fashionable fur fit for service

parts.note: U means upper-class or socially acceptable
sable is the fur of a small Asian mammal

explanation.surface: A stylish fur coat in good condition.
explanation.walkthrough: U as upper-class comes from Nancy Mitford's 'U and non-U' usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Serviceable, able to be put to work, is the sense.

clue.text: Woman seen with German recluse

parts.note: her is a pronoun for a woman
mit is the German word for with

explanation.surface: A lady seen in the company of a German is a loner.
explanation.definitionFit: One who lives alone apart from society is a synonym.

clue.text: Medicinal solution can restore health if given time

parts.note: a tin is a can

indicators.note: the cure word is given the time abbreviation inside it

parts.note: to cure is to make well again

explanation.surface: A medicine can heal if taken over time.
explanation.definitionFit: A medicine dissolved in alcohol is the pharmacist's term.
